reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: 5 week old ex 35 weeker with pyloric stenosis and electrolytes still not at target, a father who had masseter rigidity and fever under anesthesia, active vomiting with no gastric tube, and prior apnea of prematurity.

asa.rationale: Dehydration with metabolic alkalosis, ex premature infant, possible MH susceptibility.

decision.rationale: Pyloric stenosis is a medical emergency, not a surgical one. Hospitalist targets (Cl 100 or more, HCO3 under 30, normal K) are not met; alkalosis raises postoperative apnea risk. Do not keep the 1300 slot unless the 1200 BMP meets target.

redFlags.evidence: Cl 93, HCO3 33, K 3.2, pH 7.49; BMP pending 1200; surgeon asking to keep 1300.
redFlags.implication: Metabolic alkalosis causes postoperative hypoventilation and apnea.
redFlags.action: Continue resuscitation, proceed only after targets are met.

redFlags.evidence: Father: high fever and stiff jaw during childhood ear surgery, surgery stopped, never tested.
redFlags.action: Trigger free anesthetic (no succinylcholine, no volatile agents), prepared machine, dantrolene available.

redFlags.evidence: Vomited at 0930 despite NPO; no NG or OG ordered; distended fluid filled stomach on US.
redFlags.action: Pass OG and suction (supine, lateral, prone) before induction; RSI with rocuronium.

redFlags.evidence: 35 weeks GA, now about 40 weeks PMA; A&B spells with caffeine in NICU; postop apnea monitoring not ordered.
redFlags.implication: Apnea after anesthesia, worse with alkalosis and opioids.
redFlags.action: Avoid opioids (acetaminophen and local), continuous apnea and oximetry monitoring overnight.
Difficult airway equipment sized for neonates.

redFlags.evidence: NPO, D5 maintenance running, neonatal hypoglycemia history.
redFlags.action: Continue dextrose containing fluid, check glucose.

planItems.item: OG suction then RSI with rocuronium (no succinylcholine)
Trigger free TIVA or non triggering technique
Acetaminophen and surgeon local, avoid opioids
